spec_issues: The held-out set is SciTikZ-Bench (611 figures, tests/data.json -> inductionlabs/frontier-ml-tasks scitikz/private). The prompt and CONTRACT.md forbid any use of it; no trial downloaded it, a mirror, or the benchmark repo/HF tasks dataset (searched all 18 trajectories for inductionlabs/frontier-ml-tasks/frontierml.org: no hits).

The 50 public examples are SciTikZ-230K rows, explicitly allowed for training and selection (SCHEMA.md; tests/task/review.py:29-35). Trials differed (most excluded them by hash; DeepSeek 48h210 and Astra 3sl4he/5jvzxw trained on them); both are legal and the reviewer treated them consistently.

Render-and-compare selection is allowed by the review rule ('Model-driven rendering, refinement and selection are allowed', tests/task/review.py:41-42) but is not mentioned in the prompt. The top compile rates come from servers that compile candidates in-process with a bundled TeX Live or Tectonic (Fable 4pf2v7 99.8%, Fable 4mfvjr 99.5%, Astra 3dkpma 98.9%). Fable 4pf2v7 reranks with SigLIP SO400M, which is also one of the seven scoring metrics.
'Unmodified off-the-shelf weights alone fail' (tests/task/review.py:9-10) is stricter than the prompt's wording but consistent with 'Train a vision-language model'; no trial was affected.
verifier_issues: The score is the raw metric x 100 with no floor: compilation rate x geometric mean of SigLIP, CLIP, exp(-LPIPS/0.5), SSIM, 1-DreamSim, exp(-TED/0.4) and CrystalBLEU (scitikz_metric.py aggregate()). Several components saturate near 0.8-0.9 for any plausible render, so zero-shot Qwen3-VL already scores about 0.2-0.4 on the dev set ([64] in Opus 1rlvur: 0.407) and the 18 trials span only 39.6-65.1.

Overlap between the training corpus and the benchmark was checked only for the 50 dev rows and only for exact matches: scitikz_data.py:95-96 'Exact overlap only, not semantic/template deduplication or pretraining contamination detection'. SciTikZ-230K and SciTikZ-Bench come from the same pipeline, so template-level near-duplicates in the 230k training rows may reward training on more of the corpus (Opus 3mquyr trained on all of it). Not measurable from public data.

The grade page shows only the compile count and the scalar; the seven component means are not published, so it is impossible to tell whether reranking against SigLIP or SSIM moved scores beyond compile rate.
task_level.noise: Within-model wallet order is mostly flat: Fable 54.5/54.0/56.5, Gemini 51.4/53.9/52.9, Muse 41.4/44.4/43.0, Astra 52.9/57.0/59.1, Opus 56.4/57.0/65.1, DeepSeek 40.7/39.6/51.1. Run-to-run noise is visible in the agents' own measurements: Opus 3mquyr scored the same checkpoint with greedy decoding four times on the 50 dev figures and got 0.629, 0.656, 0.655 and 0.617 ([226]). On 611 figures the spread should be roughly 1-2 points. The $50 winner (Astra 3sl4he 0.57026 vs Opus 1rlvur 0.57009) is decided by 0.0002 raw and would flip under any plausible re-run. The $10 margin (Opus 56.4 vs Fable 54.5) is within noise; only the $200 Opus win (65.1 vs Astra 59.1) is clearly real.
task_level.elicitation: All six harnesses ran normally. Astra (Codex) used the most steps (596-1265) and the most model spend ($109-249) but no multi-agent or imagegen tools. Astra 3sl4he burned three of four selfchecks on startup failures and passed only at 10h49m (startup 215 s of 300 s). DeepSeek's 10bzdt trial failed two selfchecks on the 2-hour gate before it wrote a chunked decoder. Gemini runs were the re-run '-r2' versions. None of these changed a winner.
task_level.epoch_rationale: All 18 trials passed review, I found no violation the reviewer missed and no infrastructure zero, so no scoring defect changes a winner. The $50 winner is a statistical tie (Astra 0.57026 vs Opus 0.57009), but that is noise, not a defect.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: Almost all of the score is ordinary engineering: fine-tune a Qwen VLM on as much of the allowed SciTikZ-230K corpus as the wallet buys, then add serve-time compile checks, repair and candidate selection. There is no gaming of the rules. The one grader-aware choice is reranking against a metric model (Fable 4pf2v7's SigLIP reranker), which the review rule permits. The biggest single gain was Opus 3mquyr's choice of a newer base (Qwen3.5-9B) with full-corpus full-parameter SFT. No trial produced a transferable research idea.
